docs.title: op_system
docs.text:
op_system validates YAML/JSON-friendly specifications for spatial and trait-structured PDEs, nonlocal integral/mixing dynamics, compartmental flows, ODEs and stochastic reaction networks. It compiles shaped-state evaluators and publishes operator, reaction and observable contracts. Numerical consumers supply discretization and time/event integration. The core can be used directly or through a separate flepimop2 provider.

The test suite covers NumPy, concrete and traced JAX arrays, and raw PyTorch tensors. Other Array API implementations may work through array-api-compat, but should be qualified before production use.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install op-system

docs.title: Main interfaces
docs.text:
• compile_spec(...) validates, normalizes, and compiles a loaded mapping.
  • normalize_rhs(...) normalizes without compilation.
  • validate_spec(...) returns a structural validation report.
  • compile_rhs(...) creates a reusable CompiledRhs object.
  • CompiledRhs.eval_fn(...) evaluates a flat state vector.
  • CompiledRhs.pytree_eval_fn(...) evaluates shaped state mappings.
  • CompiledRhs.block_pytree_eval_fn(...) supports hierarchical block-axis vectorization using the specification's factorize_axes declaration.

Start with the model specification guide and its executable age-structured SEIR example. See the repository README for a worked example and the navigation for the specification and API references.

docs.title: Array namespace boundary
docs.text: The array namespace is selected from input arrays at call time. A numerical engine selects integration methods, while a provider adapts framework interfaces. See array namespace terminology. Keep model expressions within the documented allowlist, and validate an additional backend against the package's conformance tests before treating it as supported in a production workflow.

docs.title: Contributing and citation
docs.text:
The contributor guide covers setup, focused PRs, required checks, and support. Citation and archiving explains attribution, release identifiers, and the software-paper archive plan.

See capabilities and executable examples for current interfaces, optional dependencies, limitations and the checks that run in CI.

This analysis uses the compiled unit-transfer incidence structure, without sampling propensities or inferring physical conservation from state names.

docs.title: reaction_balances(compiled)
docs.text:
Derive conditional scalar totals from fully represented unit transfers.

Each internal incidence column has one consumed and one produced unit. Component-indicator vectors therefore give an exact integer left-nullspace basis. Source-only channels appear explicitly on the right-hand side of their component balances. Any unsupported contribution prevents all laws; omitted terms are never assigned zero flux. Propensities are not evaluated.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default compiled CompiledRhs

Compiled RHS with complete named scalar reaction artifacts.

required

Returns:

Type Description ReactionBalanceReport

Immutable identities, coverage records, declarations and assumptions.

ReactionBalanceReport

Physical interpretation and numerical/runtime realization require

ReactionBalanceReport

independent qualification; fully_covered is a structural result.

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

If compiled is not a CompiledRhs container.

Examples:

>>> from op_system import compile_spec
>>> compiled = compile_spec({
...     "kind": "transitions",
...     "state": ["S", "I"],
...     "transitions": [
...         {"name": "move", "from": "S", "to": "I", "rate": "k"},
...     ],
... })
>>> report = reaction_balances(compiled)
>>> report.fully_covered, len(report.laws)
(True, 1)
>>> report.laws[0].coefficients, report.laws[0].closed
((1, 1), True)
Source code in src/op_system/balances.py 
def reaction_balances(compiled: CompiledRhs) -> ReactionBalanceReport:
    """Derive conditional scalar totals from fully represented unit transfers.

    Each internal incidence column has one consumed and one produced unit.
    Component-indicator vectors therefore give an exact integer left-nullspace
    basis. Source-only channels appear explicitly on the right-hand side of
    their component balances. Any unsupported contribution prevents all laws;
    omitted terms are never assigned zero flux. Propensities are not evaluated.

    Args:
        compiled: Compiled RHS with complete named scalar reaction artifacts.

    Returns:
        Immutable identities, coverage records, declarations and assumptions.
        Physical interpretation and numerical/runtime realization require
        independent qualification; ``fully_covered`` is a structural result.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If ``compiled`` is not a CompiledRhs container.

    Examples:
        >>> from op_system import compile_spec
        >>> compiled = compile_spec({
        ...     "kind": "transitions",
        ...     "state": ["S", "I"],
        ...     "transitions": [
        ...         {"name": "move", "from": "S", "to": "I", "rate": "k"},
        ...     ],
        ... })
        >>> report = reaction_balances(compiled)
        >>> report.fully_covered, len(report.laws)
        (True, 1)
        >>> report.laws[0].coefficients, report.laws[0].closed
        ((1, 1), True)
    """
    if not isinstance(compiled, CompiledRhs):
        msg = "compiled must be a CompiledRhs"
        raise TypeError(msg)
    states = tuple(compiled.state_names)
    gaps = _coverage(compiled)
    components = () if gaps else _components(states, compiled.reactions)
    gaps.extend(_scientific_coverage(compiled, components))
    names = tuple(reaction.name for reaction in compiled.reactions)
    laws = (
        ()
        if gaps
        else tuple(
            ReactionBalanceLaw(
                name=f"component:{index}",
                coefficients=tuple(int(name in component) for name in states),
                reaction_names=names,
                sources=tuple(
                    ReactionBalanceSource(reaction.name, 1, reaction.to_base)
                    for reaction in compiled.reactions
                    if reaction.from_base is None and reaction.to_base in component
                ),
                assumptions=_ASSUMPTIONS,
            )
            for index, component in enumerate(components)
        )
    )
    return ReactionBalanceReport(
        states,
        laws,
        tuple(gaps),
        tuple(
            (name, compiled.state_meta[name])
            for name in states
            if name in compiled.state_meta
        ),
        tuple(compiled.axis_meta.items()),
        _ASSUMPTIONS,
    )

docs.title: compile
docs.text:
op_system.compile.

Compile normalized RHS specifications into efficient, runnable callables.

This module is domain-agnostic and intentionally does not import flepimop2.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
• Accepts NormalizedRhs (from op_system.specs) and produces a CompiledRhs object containing an eval_fn suitable for numerical backends.
  • Raises built-in exceptions with standardized messages.

docs.title: Security note
docs.text: This module uses eval() on code objects compiled from user-provided strings. To reduce risk, expressions are parsed and validated with a conservative AST whitelist, and evaluation runs with empty builtins.

docs.title: CompiledReactant(state_base, state_axes, full_axes, pinned, order) dataclass
docs.text:
Molecular reactant metadata aligned to an expanded reaction channel.

The record is numerical-array neutral. Providers combine state_axes with the enclosing reaction's channel coordinates and pinned indices to locate a state cell, then place order in their reactant-order matrix. Catalysts appear here even when their net stoichiometric change is zero.

docs.title: CompiledReaction(name, from_base, from_axes, full_axes, to_base, to_axes, sum_axes, pinned, from_pinned, propensity_fn, reactants=(), reactants_complete=False, offsets=(), to_full_axes=None, routed_axes=(), dependencies=(), propensity_order=None, dependencies_complete=False, resolved_propensity_fn=None, time_varying_params=(), independent_axes=(), uses_time=False) dataclass
docs.text:
Compiled propensity + axis bookkeeping for one named transition.

Produced from :class:op_system._reactions.ReactionArtifactIR at compile time. A firing event at from-cell index i (in the natural N-D shape given by from_axes) depletes 1 from from_base at that cell and adds 1 to to_base at the cell obtained by: keeping every axis in to_axes at i's value for that axis, and using the fixed coordinate index from pinned for every axis in pinned (this includes both axes that are wildcard on from_axes and pinned on to -- a "collapse to a fixed target" transition, where multiple source cells share one destination and the axis also appears in sum_axes -- and axes pinned on BOTH from and to, a "point-to-point" shift between two specific coordinates on the same axis, e.g. a vaccination-dose-progression transition, which do NOT appear in sum_axes since there's only ever one source value on that axis). Consumers that need a single combined scatter/reduce target (e.g. an engine applying many simultaneous firings) sum over sum_axes when depositing into to_base -- op_system does not do that summation itself, since whether/how to combine simultaneous firings across a summed axis is an execution-semantics decision for the consumer, not a compile-time one.

from_base is None for a SOURCE-ONLY (from: null) reaction -- an exogenous hazard with no compartment to deplete (e.g. cross-district case importation). A consumer must special-case this: skip every from-side depletion/clamp step and apply only the to_base scatter, using from_axes/full_axes (which are the to-side template's own axes in this case, not a nonexistent from-side one -- see ReactionArtifactIR).

An axis-wide coord_shift publishes one reaction per state template with a non-empty offsets: the destination index on each offset axis is the source index plus its step (see offsets). The destination cell is then built from to_axes (copied), pinned (fixed), and offsets (shifted), which together cover full_axes.

Examples:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from op_system import compile_spec
>>> compiled = compile_spec({
...     "kind": "transitions",
...     "state": ["S", "I"],
...     "transitions": [
...         {"name": "infect", "from": "S", "to": "I", "rate": "k"},
...     ],
... })
>>> reaction = compiled.reactions[0]
>>> float(
...     reaction.propensity_fn(
...         0.0, {"S": np.array(10.0), "I": np.array(0.0)}, k=0.2
...     )
... )
2.0
>>> reaction.time_varying_params, reaction.uses_time
((), False)

docs.title: CompiledRhs(state_names, param_names, eval_fn, meta=(lambda: MappingProxyType({}))(), operators=tuple(), factorize_axes=tuple(), block_axes=tuple(), pytree_eval_fn=None, template_shapes=None, block_pytree_eval_fn=None, block_template_shapes=None, history_requirements=tuple(), history_eval_fn=None, body_eval_fn=None, block_history_eval_fn=None, block_body_eval_fn=None, reactions=tuple(), reaction_gaps=tuple(), _rhs=None, param_meta=(lambda: MappingProxyType({}))(), state_meta=(lambda: MappingProxyType({}))(), axis_meta=(lambda: MappingProxyType({}))(), observables=(lambda: MappingProxyType({}))(), gauges=None, gauge_fix=None) dataclass
docs.text:
Container for a compiled RHS evaluation function.

Instances produced by :func:compile_rhs retain a private reference to their source :class:NormalizedRhs so the container can be pickled and re-hydrated by re-running the compile pipeline on load. eval_fn itself is a closure (and on the vectorized path captures compiled code objects), so it is dropped from the pickle and rebuilt by :func:compile_rhs in :meth:__setstate__. Round-tripping a CompiledRhs therefore costs one compile on load and yields a functionally equivalent instance whose eval_fn produces identical outputs for identical inputs.

docs.title: __getstate__()
docs.text:
Return picklable state.

The compiled eval_fn is a closure (and on the vectorized path captures compiled :class:types.CodeType objects), which is not portably picklable. Instead we serialize just the source :class:NormalizedRhs and let :meth:__setstate__ recompile.

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

If the source NormalizedRhs was not retained (i.e. the instance was constructed directly rather than via :func:compile_rhs).

Source code in src/op_system/compile.py 
def __getstate__(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return picklable state.

    The compiled ``eval_fn`` is a closure (and on the vectorized path
    captures compiled :class:`types.CodeType` objects), which is not
    portably picklable. Instead we serialize just the source
    :class:`NormalizedRhs` and let :meth:`__setstate__` recompile.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If the source ``NormalizedRhs`` was not retained
            (i.e. the instance was constructed directly rather than
            via :func:`compile_rhs`).
    """
    if self._rhs is None:
        msg = (
            "CompiledRhs is not picklable: the source NormalizedRhs was "
            "not retained. Construct via compile_rhs() to produce a "
            "picklable CompiledRhs."
        )
        raise TypeError(msg)
    return {"_rhs": self._rhs}

docs.title: __setstate__(state)
docs.text:
Restore by recompiling from the pickled :class:NormalizedRhs.

Source code in src/op_system/compile.py 
def __setstate__(self, state: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Restore by recompiling from the pickled :class:`NormalizedRhs`."""
    rhs = state["_rhs"]
    rebuilt = compile_rhs(rhs)
    # frozen+slots dataclass: bypass __setattr__ via object.__setattr__
    object.__setattr__(self, "state_names", rebuilt.state_names)
    object.__setattr__(self, "param_names", rebuilt.param_names)
    object.__setattr__(self, "param_meta", rebuilt.param_meta)
    object.__setattr__(self, "state_meta", rebuilt.state_meta)
    object.__setattr__(self, "axis_meta", rebuilt.axis_meta)
    object.__setattr__(self, "observables", rebuilt.observables)
    object.__setattr__(self, "gauges", rebuilt.gauges)
    object.__setattr__(self, "gauge_fix", rebuilt.gauge_fix)
    object.__setattr__(self, "eval_fn", rebuilt.eval_fn)
    object.__setattr__(self, "meta", rebuilt.meta)
    object.__setattr__(self, "operators", rebuilt.operators)
    object.__setattr__(self, "factorize_axes", rebuilt.factorize_axes)
    object.__setattr__(self, "block_axes", rebuilt.block_axes)
    object.__setattr__(self, "pytree_eval_fn", rebuilt.pytree_eval_fn)
    object.__setattr__(self, "template_shapes", rebuilt.template_shapes)
    object.__setattr__(self, "block_pytree_eval_fn", rebuilt.block_pytree_eval_fn)
    object.__setattr__(self, "block_template_shapes", rebuilt.block_template_shapes)
    object.__setattr__(self, "history_requirements", rebuilt.history_requirements)
    object.__setattr__(self, "history_eval_fn", rebuilt.history_eval_fn)
    object.__setattr__(self, "body_eval_fn", rebuilt.body_eval_fn)
    object.__setattr__(self, "block_history_eval_fn", rebuilt.block_history_eval_fn)
    object.__setattr__(self, "block_body_eval_fn", rebuilt.block_body_eval_fn)
    object.__setattr__(self, "reactions", rebuilt.reactions)
    object.__setattr__(self, "reaction_gaps", rebuilt.reaction_gaps)
    object.__setattr__(self, "_rhs", rhs)

def bind(
    self, params: Mapping[str, object]
) -> Callable[[object, object], Float64Array]:
    """Bind parameter values and return a 2-arg RHS: rhs(t, y) -> dydt.

    Args:
        params: Mapping of parameter names to values.

    Returns:
        A callable `rhs(t, y)` that evaluates the RHS with `params` fixed.
    """
    params_dict = dict(params)

    def rhs(t: object, y: object) -> Float64Array:
        return self.eval_fn(t, y, **params_dict)

    return rhs

docs.title: PytreeEvalFn

Bases: Protocol

Callable RHS evaluator operating on shaped PyTree state dicts.

Accepts y as a StateDict (mapping from state-template base name to a shaped array with the template's natural N-D shape) and returns a StateDict of the same structure containing the derivative. Enables the engine to skip the flatten/unflatten step entirely and expose the full tensor structure to JAX/XLA.

docs.title: compile_rhs(rhs, *, xp=None, detect_gauges=False, gauge_fix=None)
docs.text:
Compile a normalized RHS into a runnable evaluation function.

Always uses the vectorized eval path that operates on shaped buffers (one tensor expression per state template) for specs that declare axes. Specs without axes (genuinely scalar models) fall back to the scalar path. Raising :class:UnsupportedFeatureError if an axis-indexed spec cannot be vectorized, rather than silently falling back to the catastrophically slow scalar path.

The returned eval_fn is namespace-polymorphic: it infers its array namespace from the input y at call time (through array_api_compat.array_namespace), and returns arrays in that same namespace. Calling it with JAX arrays (or tracers) yields a JAX-native computation suitable for jax.jit / jax.vmap without any correctness wrapping.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rhs NormalizedRhs

Normalized RHS produced by op_system.specs.normalize_rhs.

required detect_gauges bool

False gauge_fix Mapping[str, float] | None

Positive scalar anchors for the reported scaling action.

None xp object | None

def compile_rhs(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-locals]
    rhs: NormalizedRhs,
    *,
    xp: object | None = None,
    detect_gauges: bool = False,
    gauge_fix: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
) -> CompiledRhs:
    """Compile a normalized RHS into a runnable evaluation function.

    Always uses the vectorized eval path that operates on shaped buffers
    (one tensor expression per state template) for specs that declare axes.
    Specs without axes (genuinely scalar models) fall back to the scalar path.
    Raising :class:`UnsupportedFeatureError` if an axis-indexed spec cannot be
    vectorized, rather than silently falling back to the catastrophically slow
    scalar path.

    The returned ``eval_fn`` is **namespace-polymorphic**: it infers its
    array namespace from the input ``y`` at call time
    (through ``array_api_compat.array_namespace``), and returns arrays in that same
    namespace. Calling it with JAX arrays (or tracers) yields a JAX-native
    computation suitable for ``jax.jit`` / ``jax.vmap`` without any
    correctness wrapping.

    Args:
        rhs: Normalized RHS produced by `op_system.specs.normalize_rhs`.
        detect_gauges: Opt in to conservative structural scaling detection.
        gauge_fix: Positive scalar anchors for the reported scaling action.
        xp: **Deprecated.** Formerly the compile-time array namespace.
            Now ignored — the namespace is resolved per call
            from the input ``y``. Will be removed in a future release.

    Returns:
        A `CompiledRhs` containing an `eval_fn(t, y, **params) -> dydt`.
        For axis-indexed specs the returned object also carries
        ``pytree_eval_fn`` and ``template_shapes``.  If the spec declares
        axes but the vectorizer cannot build a plan an
        ``UnsupportedFeatureError`` is raised (see bail reason in the detail
        message) rather than silently degrading to the scalar path.
    """
    _warn_on_deprecated_xp(xp)
    _validate_rhs_type(rhs)

    _validate_history_kinds(
        _history_requirements_from_ir(
            aliases_ir=rhs.aliases_ir,
            equations_ir=rhs.equations_ir,
        )
        if _reduce_ir_has_history(rhs)
        else ()
    )

    vec, plan, eval_fn, pytree_eval_fn, template_shapes = _build_primary_eval_artifacts(
        rhs
    )

    # Apply both time-varying and synth-const wrappers to ``pytree_eval_fn``
    # BEFORE ``_build_history_artifacts`` consumes it.  history_eval_fn /
    # body_eval_fn capture the pytree_eval_fn reference at construction
    # time, so any later re-wrapping would not propagate into them; that
    # would leave runtime history-body calls missing time-varying param
    # slicing and synthesized constants (e.g. __op_system_mask__* one-hot
    # arrays for pinned transition selectors).
    synth_consts: Mapping[str, object] | None = None
    if eval_fn is not None:
        eval_fn, pytree_eval_fn = _wrap_time_varying_artifacts(
            rhs=rhs,
            eval_fn=eval_fn,
            pytree_eval_fn=pytree_eval_fn,
        )
        eval_fn, pytree_eval_fn, synth_consts = _apply_synth_const_wrappers(
            rhs=rhs,
            eval_fn=eval_fn,
            pytree_eval_fn=pytree_eval_fn,
        )

    history_requirements, history_eval_fn, body_eval_fn = _build_history_artifacts(
        rhs=rhs,
        plan=plan,
        pytree_eval_fn=pytree_eval_fn,
    )

    eval_fn = _resolve_eval_fn(
        rhs=rhs,
        eval_fn=eval_fn,
        history_requirements=history_requirements,
    )

    block_axes = analyze_block_axes(rhs)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Block-stripped compile: produce a per-block-coord pytree_eval_fn by
    # stripping the first factorize axis from the RHS and re-running the
    # vectorizer.  Engines can jax.vmap this over the block axis instead
    # of baking literal axis indices that break under vmap.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    block_pytree_eval_fn, block_template_shapes = _build_block_pytree_artifacts(
        rhs=rhs,
        vec=vec,
        pytree_eval_fn=pytree_eval_fn,
        block_axes=block_axes,
        synth_consts=synth_consts,
    )

    # Build per-block history / body eval fns when both the block compile and
    # history path succeeded.  These wrap ``block_pytree_eval_fn`` exactly as
    # ``history_eval_fn`` / ``body_eval_fn`` wrap ``pytree_eval_fn``.
    block_history_eval_fn, block_body_eval_fn = _build_block_history_artifacts(
        block_pytree_eval_fn=block_pytree_eval_fn,
        history_requirements=history_requirements,
    )

    reaction_artifacts = _build_reaction_artifacts(rhs=rhs, plan=plan, vec=vec)
    compiled = CompiledRhs(
        state_names=rhs.state_names,
        param_names=tuple(rhs.param_names),
        eval_fn=eval_fn,
        meta=rhs.meta,
        param_meta=MappingProxyType(
            dict(
                cast(
                    "Mapping[str, ParameterDeclaration]",
                    rhs.meta.get("parameter_declarations", {}),
                )
            )
        ),
        state_meta=MappingProxyType(
            dict(
                cast(
                    "Mapping[str, StateDeclaration]",
                    rhs.meta.get("state_declarations", {}),
                )
            )
        ),
        axis_meta=MappingProxyType(
            _axis_declarations(
                cast("Sequence[Mapping[str, object]]", rhs.meta.get("axes", ()))
            )
        ),
        operators=_parse_operator_descriptors(rhs.meta),
        observables=MappingProxyType(_compile_observables(rhs)),

def bind(
    self, params: Mapping[str, object]
) -> Callable[[object, object], Float64Array]:
    """Bind source parameters to the coordinate derivative.

def encode(self, state: Array, *, state_axis: int = 0) -> Array:
    """Check a physical initial state eagerly before taking logarithms.

    Args:
        state: Finite floating natural state, positive in selected components.
        state_axis: Component axis, in source order.

    Returns:
        Initial state in solver coordinates. Use encode_native under JIT/AD.
    """
    xp = array_namespace(state)
    values, mask = _array_and_mask(state, self._mask, state_axis)
    valid = xp.logical_and(
        xp.all(xp.isfinite(values)),
        xp.all(xp.logical_or(xp.logical_not(mask), xp.greater(values, 0))),
    )
    _require_valid(valid, "encode")
    return self.encode_native(state, state_axis=state_axis).state

def decode(self, coordinates: GaugeCoordinates) -> tuple[Array, dict[str, object]]:
    """Recover original values using retained group coordinates.

    Args:
        coordinates: Encoded representative with its original log scales.

    Returns:
        Original flat state and complete parameter mapping. A quotient alone
        has no inverse; these retained scales select the original member.
    """
    state, remaining, logs, _ = coordinates
    xp = array_namespace(state)
    factors = xp.exp(xp.asarray(self.state_weights, dtype=state.dtype) @ logs)
    factors = xp.reshape(
        factors, (len(self.state_weights),) + (1,) * (len(state.shape) - 1)
    )
    params = {**remaining, **dict(self.fixed_values)}
    original = {
        name: xp.asarray(value, dtype=state.dtype)
        * xp.exp(
            -xp.sum(
                xp.asarray(
                    [
                        dict(generator.parameters).get(name, 0.0)
                        for generator in self.generators
                    ],
                    dtype=state.dtype,
                )
                * logs
            )
        )
        for name, value in params.items()
    }
    return state / factors, original

def encode(
    self, state: Array, parameters: Mapping[str, object]
) -> GaugeCoordinates:
    """Map natural state/parameters to the anchored representative.

    Args:
        state: Real floating flat state, with optional trailing batch axes.
        parameters: Original parameter values, including positive anchors.

    Returns:
        Representative, original group coordinates and native domain flag.
        Check ``valid`` before using a result in an inference pipeline.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If state axes or anchor shapes do not match this map.
        TypeError: If states are not real floating arrays.
    """
    if not state.shape or state.shape[0] != len(self.state_weights):
        msg = "Gauge map state axis does not match the compiled model"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    xp = array_namespace(state)
    if not xp.isdtype(state.dtype, "real floating"):
        msg = "Gauge coordinates require real floating state arrays"
        raise TypeError(msg)
    values = xp.stack([
        xp.asarray(parameters[name], dtype=state.dtype)
        for name, _ in self.fixed_values
    ])
    if len(values.shape) != 1:
        msg = "Gauge anchors must be scalar; use vmap for separate parameter draws"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    targets = xp.asarray(
        [value for _, value in self.fixed_values], dtype=state.dtype
    )
    matrix = xp.asarray(self.inverse_anchor_matrix, dtype=state.dtype)
    logs = matrix @ (xp.log(targets) - xp.log(values))
    valid = xp.all(xp.logical_and(xp.isfinite(values), values > 0))
    valid = xp.logical_and(valid, xp.all(xp.isfinite(logs)))
    weights = xp.asarray(self.state_weights, dtype=state.dtype)
    factors = xp.exp(weights @ logs)
    valid = xp.logical_and(
        valid, xp.all(xp.logical_and(xp.isfinite(factors), factors > 0))
    )
    factors = xp.reshape(
        factors, (len(self.state_weights),) + (1,) * (len(state.shape) - 1)
    )
    transformed = {
        name: xp.asarray(value, dtype=state.dtype)
        * xp.exp(
            xp.sum(
                xp.asarray(
                    [
                        dict(generator.parameters).get(name, 0.0)
                        for generator in self.generators
                    ],
                    dtype=state.dtype,
                )
                * logs
            )
        )
        for name, value in parameters.items()
        if name not in dict(self.fixed_values)
    }
    mapped_state = state * factors
    valid = xp.logical_and(valid, xp.all(xp.isfinite(mapped_state)))
    valid = xp.logical_and(
        valid,
        xp.all(xp.logical_or(xp.not_equal(mapped_state, 0), xp.equal(state, 0))),
    )
    for name, value in transformed.items():
        original = xp.asarray(parameters[name], dtype=state.dtype)
        finite = xp.all(xp.isfinite(value))
        retained = xp.all(xp.logical_or(value != 0, original == 0))
        valid = xp.logical_and(valid, xp.logical_and(finite, retained))
    return GaugeCoordinates(mapped_state, transformed, logs, valid)

def evaluate(self, parameters: Mapping[str, object]) -> object:
    """Evaluate a monomial using supplied values, without domain correction.

    Args:
        parameters: Values with native array broadcasting semantics.

    Returns:
        Product of the named powers. Negative powers require nonzero values.

    Examples:
        >>> invariant = InvariantCoordinate((("K", 1), ("c", 1)))
        >>> invariant.evaluate({"K": 4.0, "c": 3.0})
        12.0
    """
    result: object = 1.0
    for name, exponent in self.exponents:
        # Arithmetic is namespace-native for concrete values and tracers.
        result *= parameters[name] ** exponent  # type: ignore[operator]
    return result

@classmethod
def from_mapping(cls, name: str, value: object) -> ObservableDefinition:
    """Validate the bounded observable schema.

    Args:
        name: Output identifier.
        value: Mapping with expr, optional axes/reduction/units/description.

    Returns:
        Detached immutable definition.

    Raises:
        InvalidRhsSpecError: If identifiers, fields or reductions are invalid.
    """
    if not _identifier(name):
        raise InvalidRhsSpecError(detail="observable names must be identifiers")
    if not isinstance(value, Mapping) or set(value) - {
        "expr",
        "axes",
        "reduction",
        "units",
        "description",
    }:
        raise InvalidRhsSpecError(detail=f"observable {name!r} has invalid fields")
    expression = _text(value, "expr", required=True)
    axes = _axes(value.get("axes", ()))
    reduction = None
    if "reduction" in value:
        raw = value["reduction"]
        if not isinstance(raw, Mapping) or set(raw) != {"kind", "axes"}:
            raise InvalidRhsSpecError(
                detail="observable reduction needs kind and axes"
            )
        kind = raw["kind"]
        reduction_axes = _axes(raw["axes"])
        if (
            not isinstance(kind, str)
            or kind not in {"sum", "integral"}
            or not reduction_axes
        ):
            raise InvalidRhsSpecError(
                detail="observable reduction must be a nonempty sum or integral"
            )
        reduction = ObservableReduction(
            cast('Literal["sum", "integral"]', kind), reduction_axes
        )
        if set(axes) & set(reduction_axes):
            raise InvalidRhsSpecError(
                detail="observable output and reduction axes must be disjoint"
            )
    return cls(
        name,
        cast("str", expression),
        axes,
        reduction,
        _text(value, "units"),
        _text(value, "description"),
    )

Structural Array-API protocol.

Any object whose runtime type implements shape, dtype, __array_namespace__ and item satisfies this protocol. NumPy

@classmethod
def from_mapping(cls, value: object, *, size: int) -> AxisMeasure:
    """Validate a measure without inferring geometry from coordinates.

    Args:
        value: Mapping with kind, optional units, and weights for cell/quadrature.
        size: Number of axis coordinates.

    Returns:
        Immutable measure in coordinate order.

    Raises:
        InvalidRhsSpecError: If the kind, units, weights or length are invalid.
    """
    if not isinstance(size, int) or isinstance(size, bool) or size < 1:
        raise InvalidRhsSpecError(
            detail="axis measure size must be a positive integer"
        )
    if not isinstance(value, Mapping) or set(value) - {"kind", "weights", "units"}:
        raise InvalidRhsSpecError(
            detail="axis measure must contain kind, weights and/or units"
        )
    kind = value.get("kind")
    if not isinstance(kind, str) or kind not in {"counting", "cell", "quadrature"}:
        raise InvalidRhsSpecError(
            detail="axis measure kind must be counting, cell or quadrature"
        )
    if kind == "counting":
        if "weights" in value:
            raise InvalidRhsSpecError(
                detail="counting measure has unit weights; omit weights"
            )
        weights = (1.0,) * size
    else:
        raw_weights = value.get("weights")
        if not isinstance(raw_weights, (list, tuple)) or len(raw_weights) != size:
            raise InvalidRhsSpecError(
                detail="axis measure weights must match the coordinate count"
            )
        weights = tuple(_positive_weight(weight) for weight in raw_weights)
    return cls(cast("_MeasureKind", kind), weights, _optional_text(value, "units"))

docs.text:
Metadata for one block-diagonal (factorizable) axis.

A BlockAxisInfo is attached to :class:~op_system.compile.CompiledRhs for each axis declared in spec["factorize_axes"] that passes the IR separability check in :func:analyze_block_axes. Engines (e.g. the diffrax plugin) consume this to partition independent solves with jax.vmap over the block axis.

Attributes:

Name Type Description name str

Axis name string (e.g. "loc").

size int

Number of elements along the axis.

state_axis_pos dict[str, int]

Maps each state-template base name to the integer position of this axis within that template's shape tuple. Only templates that carry this axis appear in the dict.

param_axis_pos dict[str, int | None]

Maps each shaped parameter name to the integer position of this axis within the actual runtime array that the engine passes to the eval function, or None if the parameter does not carry this axis (broadcast). For non-time-varying shaped parameters the position is the index in the parameter's axis tuple. For time-varying parameters the runtime array has time prepended at index 0, so the position equals the index of the block axis in the full (time, *spatial_axes) tuple. Parameters that are entirely scalar (not shaped) do not appear in this dict and are always broadcast.

Note

BlockAxisInfo uses dict fields and therefore cannot be used as a hash key. It is stored on :class:~op_system.compile.CompiledRhs with hash=False and is fully pickle-stable.

Examples:

>>> info = BlockAxisInfo(
...     name="loc",
...     size=3,
...     state_axis_pos={"S": 1, "I": 1, "R": 1},
...     param_axis_pos={"rho": 0, "beta": None},
... )
>>> info.name
'loc'
>>> info.size
3
>>> info.state_axis_pos["S"]
1
>>> info.param_axis_pos["rho"]
0
>>> info.param_axis_pos["beta"] is None
True

docs.text:
Compiled propensity + axis bookkeeping for one named transition.

Produced from :class:op_system._reactions.ReactionArtifactIR at compile time. A firing event at from-cell index i (in the natural N-D shape given by from_axes) depletes 1 from from_base at that cell and adds 1 to to_base at the cell obtained by: keeping every axis in to_axes at i's value for that axis, and using the fixed coordinate index from pinned for every axis in pinned (this includes both axes that are wildcard on from_axes and pinned on to -- a "collapse to a fixed target" transition, where multiple source cells share one destination and the axis also appears in sum_axes -- and axes pinned on BOTH from and to, a "point-to-point" shift between two specific coordinates on the same axis, e.g. a vaccination-dose-progression transition, which do NOT appear in sum_axes since there's only ever one source value on that axis). Consumers that need a single combined scatter/reduce target (e.g. an engine applying many simultaneous firings) sum over sum_axes when depositing into to_base -- op_system does not do that summation itself, since whether/how to combine simultaneous firings across a summed axis is an execution-semantics decision for the consumer, not a compile-time one.

from_base is None for a SOURCE-ONLY (from: null) reaction -- an exogenous hazard with no compartment to deplete (e.g. cross-district case importation). A consumer must special-case this: skip every from-side depletion/clamp step and apply only the to_base scatter, using from_axes/full_axes (which are the to-side template's own axes in this case, not a nonexistent from-side one -- see ReactionArtifactIR).

An axis-wide coord_shift publishes one reaction per state template with a non-empty offsets: the destination index on each offset axis is the source index plus its step (see offsets). The destination cell is then built from to_axes (copied), pinned (fixed), and offsets (shifted), which together cover full_axes.

Examples:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from op_system import compile_spec
>>> compiled = compile_spec({
...     "kind": "transitions",
...     "state": ["S", "I"],
...     "transitions": [
...         {"name": "infect", "from": "S", "to": "I", "rate": "k"},
...     ],
... })
>>> reaction = compiled.reactions[0]
>>> float(
...     reaction.propensity_fn(
...         0.0, {"S": np.array(10.0), "I": np.array(0.0)}, k=0.2
...     )
... )
2.0
>>> reaction.time_varying_params, reaction.uses_time
((), False)

Container for a compiled RHS evaluation function.

Instances produced by :func:compile_rhs retain a private reference to their source :class:NormalizedRhs so the container can be pickled and re-hydrated by re-running the compile pipeline on load. eval_fn itself is a closure (and on the vectorized path captures compiled code objects), so it is dropped from the pickle and rebuilt by :func:compile_rhs in :meth:__setstate__. def __getstate__(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return picklable state.

    The compiled ``eval_fn`` is a closure (and on the vectorized path
    captures compiled :class:`types.CodeType` objects), which is not
    portably picklable. Instead we serialize just the source
    :class:`NormalizedRhs` and let :meth:`__setstate__` recompile.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If the source ``NormalizedRhs`` was not retained
            (i.e. the instance was constructed directly rather than
            via :func:`compile_rhs`).
    """
    if self._rhs is None:
        msg = (
            "CompiledRhs is not picklable: the source NormalizedRhs was "
            "not retained. Construct via compile_rhs() to produce a "
            "picklable CompiledRhs."
        )
        raise TypeError(msg)
    return {"_rhs": self._rhs}

def bind(
    self, params: Mapping[str, object]
) -> Callable[[object, object], Float64Array]:
    """Bind parameter values and return a 2-arg RHS: rhs(t, y) -> dydt.

    Args:
        params: Mapping of parameter names to values.

    Returns:
        A callable `rhs(t, y)` that evaluates the RHS with `params` fixed.
    """
    params_dict = dict(params)

    def rhs(t: object, y: object) -> Float64Array:
        return self.eval_fn(t, y, **params_dict)

    return rhs

def decode(self, coordinates: GaugeCoordinates) -> tuple[Array, dict[str, object]]:
    """Recover original values using retained group coordinates.

    Args:
        coordinates: Encoded representative with its original log scales.

    Returns:
        Original flat state and complete parameter mapping. A quotient alone
        has no inverse; these retained scales select the original member.
    """
    state, remaining, logs, _ = coordinates
    xp = array_namespace(state)
    factors = xp.exp(xp.asarray(self.state_weights, dtype=state.dtype) @ logs)
    factors = xp.reshape(
        factors, (len(self.state_weights),) + (1,) * (len(state.shape) - 1)
    )
    params = {**remaining, **dict(self.fixed_values)}
    original = {
        name: xp.asarray(value, dtype=state.dtype)
        * xp.exp(
            -xp.sum(
                xp.asarray(
                    [
                        dict(generator.parameters).get(name, 0.0)
                        for generator in self.generators
                    ],
                    dtype=state.dtype,
                )
                * logs
            )
        )
        for name, value in params.items()
    }
    return state / factors, original

def encode(
    self, state: Array, parameters: Mapping[str, object]
) -> GaugeCoordinates:
    """Map natural state/parameters to the anchored representative.

    Args:
        state: Real floating flat state, with optional trailing batch axes.
        parameters: Original parameter values, including positive anchors.

    Returns:
        Representative, original group coordinates and native domain flag.
        Check ``valid`` before using a result in an inference pipeline.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If state axes or anchor shapes do not match this map.
        TypeError: If states are not real floating arrays.
    """
    if not state.shape or state.shape[0] != len(self.state_weights):
        msg = "Gauge map state axis does not match the compiled model"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    xp = array_namespace(state)
    if not xp.isdtype(state.dtype, "real floating"):
        msg = "Gauge coordinates require real floating state arrays"
        raise TypeError(msg)
    values = xp.stack([
        xp.asarray(parameters[name], dtype=state.dtype)
        for name, _ in self.fixed_values
    ])
    if len(values.shape) != 1:
        msg = "Gauge anchors must be scalar; use vmap for separate parameter draws"
        raise ValueError(msg)
    targets = xp.asarray(
        [value for _, value in self.fixed_values], dtype=state.dtype
    )
    matrix = xp.asarray(self.inverse_anchor_matrix, dtype=state.dtype)
    logs = matrix @ (xp.log(targets) - xp.log(values))
    valid = xp.all(xp.logical_and(xp.isfinite(values), values > 0))
    valid = xp.logical_and(valid, xp.all(xp.isfinite(logs)))
    weights = xp.asarray(self.state_weights, dtype=state.dtype)
    factors = xp.exp(weights @ logs)
    valid = xp.logical_and(
        valid, xp.all(xp.logical_and(xp.isfinite(factors), factors > 0))
    )
    factors = xp.reshape(
        factors, (len(self.state_weights),) + (1,) * (len(state.shape) - 1)
    )
    transformed = {
        name: xp.asarray(value, dtype=state.dtype)
        * xp.exp(
            xp.sum(
                xp.asarray(
                    [
                        dict(generator.parameters).get(name, 0.0)
                        for generator in self.generators
                    ],
                    dtype=state.dtype,
                )
                * logs
            )
        )
        for name, value in parameters.items()
        if name not in dict(self.fixed_values)
    }
    mapped_state = state * factors
    valid = xp.logical_and(valid, xp.all(xp.isfinite(mapped_state)))
    valid = xp.logical_and(
        valid,
        xp.all(xp.logical_or(xp.not_equal(mapped_state, 0), xp.equal(state, 0))),
    )
    for name, value in transformed.items():
        original = xp.asarray(parameters[name], dtype=state.dtype)
        finite = xp.all(xp.isfinite(value))
        retained = xp.all(xp.logical_or(value != 0, original == 0))
        valid = xp.logical_and(valid, xp.logical_and(finite, retained))
    return GaugeCoordinates(mapped_state, transformed, logs, valid)

def evaluate(self, parameters: Mapping[str, object]) -> object:
    """Evaluate a monomial using supplied values, without domain correction.

    Args:
        parameters: Values with native array broadcasting semantics.

    Returns:
        Product of the named powers. Negative powers require nonzero values.

    Examples:
        >>> invariant = InvariantCoordinate((("K", 1), ("c", 1)))
        >>> invariant.evaluate({"K": 4.0, "c": 3.0})
        12.0
    """
    result: object = 1.0
    for name, exponent in self.exponents:
        # Arithmetic is namespace-native for concrete values and tracers.
        result *= parameters[name] ** exponent  # type: ignore[operator]
    return result

@classmethod
def from_mapping(cls, name: str, value: object) -> ObservableDefinition:
    """Validate the bounded observable schema.

    Args:
        name: Output identifier.
        value: Mapping with expr, optional axes/reduction/units/description.

    Returns:
        Detached immutable definition.

    Raises:
        InvalidRhsSpecError: If identifiers, fields or reductions are invalid.
    """
    if not _identifier(name):
        raise InvalidRhsSpecError(detail="observable names must be identifiers")
    if not isinstance(value, Mapping) or set(value) - {
        "expr",
        "axes",
        "reduction",
        "units",
        "description",
    }:
        raise InvalidRhsSpecError(detail=f"observable {name!r} has invalid fields")
    expression = _text(value, "expr", required=True)
    axes = _axes(value.get("axes", ()))
    reduction = None
    if "reduction" in value:
        raw = value["reduction"]
        if not isinstance(raw, Mapping) or set(raw) != {"kind", "axes"}:
            raise InvalidRhsSpecError(
                detail="observable reduction needs kind and axes"
            )
        kind = raw["kind"]
        reduction_axes = _axes(raw["axes"])
        if (
            not isinstance(kind, str)
            or kind not in {"sum", "integral"}
            or not reduction_axes
        ):
            raise InvalidRhsSpecError(
                detail="observable reduction must be a nonempty sum or integral"
            )
        reduction = ObservableReduction(
            cast('Literal["sum", "integral"]', kind), reduction_axes
        )
        if set(axes) & set(reduction_axes):
            raise InvalidRhsSpecError(
                detail="observable output and reduction axes must be disjoint"
            )
    return cls(
        name,
        cast("str", expression),
        axes,
        reduction,
        _text(value, "units"),
        _text(value, "description"),
    )

        _optional_text(value, "units"),
        _optional_text(value, "description"),
        fixed,
    )

@classmethod
def from_mapping(cls, value: object) -> ParameterSupport:
    """Parse a domain name or bounded-domain mapping.

    Args:
        value: Domain string or mapping with kind, lower and upper.

    Returns:
        Immutable support declaration.

    Raises:
        InvalidRhsSpecError: If the domain or bounds are invalid.
    """
    if isinstance(value, str) and value in {"real", "positive", "unit_interval"}:
        return cls(cast("_SupportKind", value))
    if not isinstance(value, Mapping) or set(value) != {"kind", "lower", "upper"}:
        raise InvalidRhsSpecError(
            detail=(
                "parameter support must be real, positive, unit_interval, "
                "or a bounded mapping with kind, lower and upper"
            )
        )
    lower = _finite_bound(value["lower"])
    upper = _finite_bound(value["upper"])
    if value["kind"] != "bounded" or lower >= upper:
        raise InvalidRhsSpecError(
            detail="bounded parameter support requires finite numeric lower < upper"
        )
    return cls("bounded", float(lower), float(upper))

def __post_init__(self) -> None:
    """Validate controls.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a tolerance or finite-difference step is invalid.
    """
    for name in (
        "rtol",
        "atol",
        "derivative_rtol",
        "derivative_atol",
        "derivative_step",
    ):
        value = getattr(self, name)
        numeric = isinstance(value, Real) and not isinstance(value, bool)
        if (
            not numeric
            or not math.isfinite(value)
            or value < 0
            or (name == "derivative_step" and value == 0)
        ):
            bound = "positive" if name == "derivative_step" else "non-negative"
            msg = f"{name} must be finite and {bound}"
            raise ValueError(msg)

docs.title: ReactionGap(origin, name, source, target, reason) dataclass
docs.text:
Model dynamics that publish no compiled reaction artifact.

A consumer that executes only CompiledRhs.reactions (for example a pure stochastic simulation) silently loses these dynamics. An empty CompiledRhs.reaction_gaps means every transition has an artifact.

Attributes:

Name Type Description origin str

Where the dynamics come from in the spec, such as transitions[2], chain[0].forward[1], or equations for an expr spec.

name str | None

The transition's name, or None when it has none.

source str | None

The transition's from selector, or None for a source-only transition or an expr spec.

target str | None

The transition's to selector, or None for an expr spec.

reason str

Why no artifact exists:

  • unnamed: the transition has no name.
  • target_axis_not_on_source: to has a wildcard axis that from lacks.
  • rate_axis_out_of_scope: the rate has a free axis outside the reaction's channel axes.
  • unsupported_layout: the compiled RHS has no vectorized state layout to index propensities against.
  • unresolved_alias: the rate still references an alias after inlining: one on a reference cycle, a templated alias referenced by bare name, or a declaration out of scope for inlining.
  • compile_failed: the propensity could not be lowered or its coordinates could not be resolved.
  • gauge_fix_requires_jump_contract: equation/output covariance does not verify a jump process's distribution. Gauge-fixed models omit reaction exports until a separate jump contract is supplied.
  • expr_spec: an expr spec, whose equations are not decomposed into transitions.

def encode(self, state: Array, *, state_axis: int = 0) -> Array:
    """Check a physical initial state eagerly before taking logarithms.

    Args:
        state: Finite floating natural state, positive in selected components.
        state_axis: Component axis, in source order.

    Returns:
        Initial state in solver coordinates. Use encode_native under JIT/AD.
    """
    xp = array_namespace(state)
    values, mask = _array_and_mask(state, self._mask, state_axis)
    valid = xp.logical_and(
        xp.all(xp.isfinite(values)),
        xp.all(xp.logical_or(xp.logical_not(mask), xp.greater(values, 0))),
    )
    _require_valid(valid, "encode")
    return self.encode_native(state, state_axis=state_axis).state

@classmethod
def from_mapping(cls, value: object) -> StateDeclaration:
    """Validate a state annotation without changing its equations.

    Args:
        value: Mapping of representation, units, description and measure_axes.

    Returns:
        Immutable declaration; omitted information remains unknown.

    Raises:
        InvalidRhsSpecError: If fields or their values are invalid.
    """
    if not isinstance(value, Mapping) or set(value) - {
        "representation",
        "units",
        "description",
        "measure_axes",
        "scale",
    }:
        raise InvalidRhsSpecError(
            detail="state metadata contains unknown fields or is not a mapping"
        )
    scale = value.get("scale", "identity")
    if not isinstance(scale, str) or scale not in {"identity", "log"}:
        raise InvalidRhsSpecError(detail="state scale must be identity or log")
    representation = value.get("representation")
    if "representation" in value and (
        not isinstance(representation, str)
        or representation
        not in {"counts", "cell_mass", "density", "concentration", "cumulative"}
    ):
        raise InvalidRhsSpecError(
            detail=(
                "state representation must be counts, cell_mass, density, "
                "concentration or cumulative"
            )
        )
    measure_axes = None
    if "measure_axes" in value:
        axes = value["measure_axes"]
        if (
            not isinstance(axes, (list, tuple))
            or any(not isinstance(axis, str) or not axis.strip() for axis in axes)
            or len(set(axes)) != len(axes)
        ):
            raise InvalidRhsSpecError(
                detail="state measure_axes must list unique nonempty axis names"
            )
        measure_axes = tuple(axes)
        if representation in {"counts", "cell_mass", "cumulative"} and measure_axes:
            raise InvalidRhsSpecError(
                detail="extensive states do not require measure weights"
            )
    return cls(
        cast("_Representation | None", representation),
        _optional_text(value, "units"),
        _optional_text(value, "description"),
        measure_axes,
        cast('Literal["identity", "log"]', scale),
    )

def __str__(self) -> str:
    """
    Return the compact string form.

    Returns:
        Compact state string.

    Examples:
        >>> str(StateString(name="S", dims=()))
        'S'
        >>> str(StateString(name="R", dims=("age",)))
        'R[age]'
        >>> str(StateString(name="R", dims=("age", "vax")))
        'R[age,vax]'
        >>> str(StateString(name="lambda", dims=("age", "vax", "state")))
        'lambda[age,vax,state]'
    """
    if not self.dims:
        return self.name
    dims = ",".join(self.dims)
    return f"{self.name}[{dims}]"

def array_namespace(value: object) -> Any:  # ruff: ignore[any-type]
    """Return an Array-API-compatible namespace for ``value``.

    ``array-api-compat`` recognizes both arrays that implement
    ``__array_namespace__`` and native arrays such as ``torch.Tensor`` that
    need a compatibility namespace. Optional backends are imported only when
    one of their arrays is supplied.

    Args:
        value: Numerical array whose namespace should be selected.

    Returns:
        The Array-API-compatible namespace for ``value``.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If ``value`` is not a supported array object.
    """
    try:
        return _array_namespace(value)
    except TypeError as error:
        msg = (
            "op_system numerical inputs must be supported array objects; "
            f"got {type(value).__name__}."
        )
        raise TypeError(msg) from error

def axis_kernel_generator_rhs(
    state: Any,  # ruff: ignore[any-type]
    generator: Any,  # ruff: ignore[any-type]
    *,
    axis: int,
    velocity: Any = 1.0,  # ruff: ignore[any-type]
) -> Any:  # ruff: ignore[any-type]
    """Return ``velocity * state @ generator`` applied along ``axis``.

    Args:
        state: Array with the kernel axis at position ``axis``.
        generator: Square matrix over the kernel axis; rows are sources.
        axis: Position of the kernel axis in ``state``.
        velocity: Scalar multiplier (for example a waning rate).

    Returns:
        The derivative contribution, with the same shape as ``state``.
    """
    xp = array_namespace(state)
    moved = xp.moveaxis(state, axis, -1)
    return xp.moveaxis(velocity * (moved @ generator), -1, axis)

def axis_kernel_redistribute(
    flux: Any,  # ruff: ignore[any-type]
    kernel: Any,  # ruff: ignore[any-type]
    *,
    axis: int = -1,
) -> Any:  # ruff: ignore[any-type]
    """Return ``flux @ kernel - flux`` along ``axis`` for a transferred flux.

    Args:
        flux: Per-coordinate flux already moved by an ordinary transfer.
        kernel: Row-stochastic matrix over the kernel axis.
        axis: Position of the kernel axis in ``flux``.

    Returns:
        The redistribution to add to the target slice.
    """
    xp = array_namespace(flux)
    moved = xp.moveaxis(flux, axis, -1)
    return xp.moveaxis(moved @ kernel - moved, -1, axis)

Always uses the vectorized eval path that operates on shaped buffers (one tensor expression per state template) for specs that declare axes. Specs without axes (genuinely scalar models) fall back to the scalar path. Calling it with JAX arrays (or tracers) yields a JAX-native computation suitable for jax.jit / jax.vmap without any correctness wrapping.

def compile_rhs(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-locals]
    rhs: NormalizedRhs,
    *,
    xp: object | None = None,
    detect_gauges: bool = False,
    gauge_fix: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
) -> CompiledRhs:
    """Compile a normalized RHS into a runnable evaluation function.

    Always uses the vectorized eval path that operates on shaped buffers
    (one tensor expression per state template) for specs that declare axes.
    Specs without axes (genuinely scalar models) fall back to the scalar path.
    Raising :class:`UnsupportedFeatureError` if an axis-indexed spec cannot be
    vectorized, rather than silently falling back to the catastrophically slow
    scalar path.

    The returned ``eval_fn`` is **namespace-polymorphic**: it infers its
    array namespace from the input ``y`` at call time
    (through ``array_api_compat.array_namespace``), and returns arrays in that same
    namespace. Calling it with JAX arrays (or tracers) yields a JAX-native
    computation suitable for ``jax.jit`` / ``jax.vmap`` without any
    correctness wrapping.

    Args:
        rhs: Normalized RHS produced by `op_system.specs.normalize_rhs`.
        detect_gauges: Opt in to conservative structural scaling detection.
        gauge_fix: Positive scalar anchors for the reported scaling action.
        xp: **Deprecated.** Formerly the compile-time array namespace.
            Now ignored — the namespace is resolved per call
            from the input ``y``. Will be removed in a future release.

    Returns:
        A `CompiledRhs` containing an `eval_fn(t, y, **params) -> dydt`.
        For axis-indexed specs the returned object also carries
        ``pytree_eval_fn`` and ``template_shapes``.  If the spec declares
        axes but the vectorizer cannot build a plan an
        ``UnsupportedFeatureError`` is raised (see bail reason in the detail
        message) rather than silently degrading to the scalar path.
    """
    _warn_on_deprecated_xp(xp)
    _validate_rhs_type(rhs)

    _validate_history_kinds(
        _history_requirements_from_ir(
            aliases_ir=rhs.aliases_ir,
            equations_ir=rhs.equations_ir,
        )
        if _reduce_ir_has_history(rhs)
        else ()
    )

    vec, plan, eval_fn, pytree_eval_fn, template_shapes = _build_primary_eval_artifacts(
        rhs
    )

    # Apply both time-varying and synth-const wrappers to ``pytree_eval_fn``
    # BEFORE ``_build_history_artifacts`` consumes it.  history_eval_fn /
    # body_eval_fn capture the pytree_eval_fn reference at construction
    # time, so any later re-wrapping would not propagate into them; that
    # would leave runtime history-body calls missing time-varying param
    # slicing and synthesized constants (e.g. __op_system_mask__* one-hot
    # arrays for pinned transition selectors).
    synth_consts: Mapping[str, object] | None = None
    if eval_fn is not None:
        eval_fn, pytree_eval_fn = _wrap_time_varying_artifacts(
            rhs=rhs,
            eval_fn=eval_fn,
            pytree_eval_fn=pytree_eval_fn,
        )
        eval_fn, pytree_eval_fn, synth_consts = _apply_synth_const_wrappers(
            rhs=rhs,
            eval_fn=eval_fn,
            pytree_eval_fn=pytree_eval_fn,
        )

    history_requirements, history_eval_fn, body_eval_fn = _build_history_artifacts(
        rhs=rhs,
        plan=plan,
        pytree_eval_fn=pytree_eval_fn,
    )

    eval_fn = _resolve_eval_fn(
        rhs=rhs,
        eval_fn=eval_fn,
        history_requirements=history_requirements,
    )

    block_axes = analyze_block_axes(rhs)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Block-stripped compile: produce a per-block-coord pytree_eval_fn by
    # stripping the first factorize axis from the RHS and re-running the
    # vectorizer.  Engines can jax.vmap this over the block axis instead
    # of baking literal axis indices that break under vmap.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    block_pytree_eval_fn, block_template_shapes = _build_block_pytree_artifacts(
        rhs=rhs,
        vec=vec,
        pytree_eval_fn=pytree_eval_fn,
        block_axes=block_axes,
        synth_consts=synth_consts,
    )

    # Build per-block history / body eval fns when both the block compile and
    # history path succeeded.  These wrap ``block_pytree_eval_fn`` exactly as
    # ``history_eval_fn`` / ``body_eval_fn`` wrap ``pytree_eval_fn``.
    block_history_eval_fn, block_body_eval_fn = _build_block_history_artifacts(
        block_pytree_eval_fn=block_pytree_eval_fn,
        history_requirements=history_requirements,
    )

    reaction_artifacts = _build_reaction_artifacts(rhs=rhs, plan=plan, vec=vec)
    compiled = CompiledRhs(
        state_names=rhs.state_names,
        param_names=tuple(rhs.param_names),
        eval_fn=eval_fn,
        meta=rhs.meta,
        param_meta=MappingProxyType(
            dict(
                cast(
                    "Mapping[str, ParameterDeclaration]",
                    rhs.meta.get("parameter_declarations", {}),
                )
            )
        ),
        state_meta=MappingProxyType(
            dict(
                cast(
                    "Mapping[str, StateDeclaration]",
                    rhs.meta.get("state_declarations", {}),
                )
            )
        ),
        axis_meta=MappingProxyType(
            _axis_declarations(
                cast("Sequence[Mapping[str, object]]", rhs.meta.get("axes", ()))
            )
        ),
        operators=_parse_operator_descriptors(rhs.meta),
        observables=MappingProxyType(_compile_observables(rhs)),
        factorize_axes=_parse_factorize_axes(rhs.meta),
        block_axes=block_axes,
        pytree_eval_fn=pytree_eval_fn,
        template_shapes=template_shapes,
        block_pytree_eval_fn=block_pytree_eval_fn,
        block_template_shapes=block_template_shapes,
        history_requirements=history_requirements,
        history_eval_fn=history_eval_fn,
        body_eval_fn=body_eval_fn,
        block_history_eval_fn=block_history_eval_fn,
        block_body_eval_fn=block_body_eval_fn,
        reactions=reaction_artifacts.reactions,
        reaction_gaps=reaction_artifacts.gaps,
        _rhs=rhs,
    )

    return _gauge_options(compiled, detect=detect_gauges, anchors=gauge_fix)

def compile_spec(  # ruff: ignore[non-empty-init-module]
    spec: dict[str, object],
    *,
    xp: object | None = None,
    backend: Literal["numpy", "jax"] = DEFAULT_ARRAY_BACKEND,
    detect_gauges: bool = False,
    gauge_fix: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
) -> CompiledRhs:
    """
    Validate, normalize, and compile a RHS specification in one call.

    This is the recommended public entrypoint for most users and adapters.

    The compiled ``eval_fn`` is **namespace-polymorphic**: it infers its
    array namespace from the input ``y`` at call time
    (through ``array_api_compat.array_namespace``), so one callable handles
    NumPy, JAX (concrete and traced), and other qualified array namespaces
    natively. This selects array operations; a downstream numerical engine
    separately selects integration methods. No compile-time namespace
    selection is required.

    Args:
        spec: Raw RHS specification mapping (YAML/JSON friendly).
        detect_gauges: Opt in to conservative structural scaling detection.
        gauge_fix: Positive scalar anchors for the reported scaling action.
        xp: **Deprecated.** Formerly the compile-time array namespace.
            Now ignored — see ``compile_rhs`` for details.
            Will be removed in a future release.
        backend: **Deprecated.** Formerly selected the compile-time
            array namespace (``"numpy"`` or ``"jax"``). Now ignored. Will be
            removed in a future release.

    Returns:
        CompiledRhs: Runnable RHS callable container.

    Examples:
        >>> import numpy as np
        >>> compiled = compile_spec({
        ...     "kind": "expr",
        ...     "state": ["x"],
        ...     "equations": {"x": "-rate*x"},
        ... })
        >>> compiled.template_shapes
        {'x': ()}
        >>> compiled.eval_fn(0.0, np.array([4.0]), rate=0.5).tolist()
        [-2.0]
    """
    if xp is not None or backend != DEFAULT_ARRAY_BACKEND:
        warnings.warn(
            "compile_spec(xp=..., backend=...) is deprecated and ignored. "
            "The compiled eval_fn now infers its array namespace from the "
            "input `y` at call time; pass JAX arrays for a JAX-native call, "
            "NumPy arrays for a NumPy call, or Torch tensors for a Torch "
            "call. These kwargs will be removed in a future release.",
            DeprecationWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )

    rhs = normalize_rhs(spec)
    return compile_rhs(rhs, detect_gauges=detect_gauges, gauge_fix=gauge_fix)

docs.title: jump_integral_generator(kernel, *, axis_type, direction='both', boundary='reflecting', quadrature_weights=None)
docs.text:
Build the conservative row-source generator for a jump kernel.

kernel[i, j] is the non-negative rate density from source coordinate i to target coordinate j. Its diagonal is ignored. up keeps only j > i; down keeps only j < i; both keeps every off-diagonal entry. For a continuous axis each target column j is multiplied by quadrature_weights[j] before the diagonal loss is set.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default kernel Any

Square source-by-target rate-density matrix.

required axis_type str

categorical, ordinal, or continuous.

required direction str

Permitted movement in declared coordinate order.

'both' boundary str

Boundary contract. Only reflecting is currently defined.

'reflecting' quadrature_weights Any | None

Positive target weights required for continuous axes and forbidden for categorical or ordinal axes.

None

Returns:

Type Description Any

A generator in the kernel's Array-API namespace. Rows sum to zero.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If static choices, shapes, or quadrature usage are invalid.

Notes

Call :func:validate_jump_integral_kernel with concrete parameter values at an orchestration boundary to check finiteness and signs. This builder deliberately keeps array values dynamic under transforms.

Source code in src/op_system/_jump_integral.py 
def jump_integral_generator(
    kernel: Any,  # ruff: ignore[any-type]
    *,
    axis_type: str,
    direction: str = "both",
    boundary: str = "reflecting",
    quadrature_weights: Any | None = None,  # ruff: ignore[any-type]
) -> Any:  # ruff: ignore[any-type]
    """Build the conservative row-source generator for a jump kernel.

    ``kernel[i, j]`` is the non-negative rate density from source coordinate
    ``i`` to target coordinate ``j``. Its diagonal is ignored. ``up`` keeps
    only ``j > i``; ``down`` keeps only ``j < i``; ``both`` keeps every
    off-diagonal entry. For a continuous axis each target column ``j`` is
    multiplied by ``quadrature_weights[j]`` before the diagonal loss is set.

    Args:
        kernel: Square source-by-target rate-density matrix.
        axis_type: ``categorical``, ``ordinal``, or ``continuous``.
        direction: Permitted movement in declared coordinate order.
        boundary: Boundary contract. Only ``reflecting`` is currently defined.
        quadrature_weights: Positive target weights required for continuous
            axes and forbidden for categorical or ordinal axes.

    Returns:
        A generator in the kernel's Array-API namespace. Rows sum to zero.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If static choices, shapes, or quadrature usage are invalid.

    Notes:
        Call :func:`validate_jump_integral_kernel` with concrete parameter
        values at an orchestration boundary to check finiteness and signs.
        This builder deliberately keeps array values dynamic under transforms.
    """
    _validate_static_contract(
        axis_type=axis_type,
        direction=direction,
        boundary=boundary,
    )
    if kernel.ndim != 2 or kernel.shape[0] != kernel.shape[1]:
        msg = "jump_integral kernel must be square"
        raise ValueError(msg)

    xp = array_namespace(kernel)
    upper = xp.triu(xp.ones_like(kernel, dtype=xp.bool), k=1)
    lower = xp.tril(xp.ones_like(kernel, dtype=xp.bool), k=-1)
    if direction == "up":
        allowed = upper
    elif direction == "down":
        allowed = lower
    else:
        allowed = xp.logical_or(upper, lower)
    rates = xp.where(allowed, kernel, xp.zeros_like(kernel))

    if axis_type == "continuous":
        if quadrature_weights is None:
            msg = "continuous jump_integral axes require quadrature_weights"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        weights = xp.asarray(
            quadrature_weights,
            dtype=kernel.dtype,
            **_device_kwargs(kernel),
        )
        if weights.ndim != 1 or weights.shape[0] != kernel.shape[0]:
            msg = "quadrature_weights must have one entry per kernel target"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        rates *= xp.reshape(weights, (1, weights.shape[0]))
    elif quadrature_weights is not None:
        msg = "quadrature_weights are only valid for continuous jump_integral axes"
        raise ValueError(msg)

    row_sums = xp.sum(rates, axis=1)
    identity = xp.eye(
        kernel.shape[0],
        dtype=kernel.dtype,
        **_device_kwargs(kernel),
    )
    return rates - identity * xp.reshape(row_sums, (row_sums.shape[0], 1))

        axis: Position of the jump axis in ``state``.
        axis_type: ``categorical``, ``ordinal``, or ``continuous``.
        rate: Scalar multiplier with inverse-time units after any continuous
            target quadrature has been applied.
        direction: ``up``, ``down``, or ``both``.
        boundary: Boundary contract; currently only ``reflecting``.
        quadrature_weights: Target quadrature weights for continuous axes.

    Returns:
        Derivative contribution with the same shape as ``state``.
    """
    generator = jump_integral_generator(
        kernel,
        axis_type=axis_type,
        direction=direction,
        boundary=boundary,
        quadrature_weights=quadrature_weights,
    )
    return axis_kernel_generator_rhs(state, generator, axis=axis, velocity=rate)

def normalize_expr_rhs(spec: Mapping[str, Any]) -> ExprRhs:  # ruff: ignore[complex-structure, too-many-locals, too-many-statements]
    """Normalize an expression-based RHS specification.

    Args:
        spec: Raw RHS specification mapping.

    Returns:
        Backend-facing normalized RHS representation.

    Raises:
        InvalidRhsSpecError: If validation fails.
    """
    state_raw = _ensure_str_list(spec.get("state"), name="state")
    if len(state_raw) != len(set(state_raw)):
        raise InvalidRhsSpecError(detail="state contains duplicate names")

    equations_map = spec.get("equations")
    if not isinstance(equations_map, dict):
        raise InvalidRhsSpecError(detail="equations must be a mapping of state->expr")

    equations_map = {_normalize_bracket_key(k): v for k, v in equations_map.items()}

    time_axis_name = _resolve_time_axis_name(spec)
    axes_meta = _normalize_axes(spec.get("axes"), time_axis_name=time_axis_name)
    meta_parts = _normalize_common_meta(
        spec,
        axis_names={"subgroup"} | {ax["name"] for ax in axes_meta},
        state_set=set(state_raw),
        operator_state_set=set(state_raw),
        axes=axes_meta,
    )

    meta: dict[str, Any] = {
        "axes": axes_meta,
        "state_axes": meta_parts[1],
        "kernels": meta_parts[2],
        "operators": meta_parts[3],
    }
    meta["op_system_may_have_history"] = _may_have_history(spec)
    for reserved_key in ("sources", "couplings", "constraints"):
        if reserved_key in spec:
            meta[reserved_key] = spec.get(reserved_key)

    state_expanded, state_template_map = _expand_state_templates(
        state_raw, axes=axes_meta
    )
    if len(state_expanded) != len(set(state_expanded)):
        raise InvalidRhsSpecError(detail="expanded state contains duplicates")

    _validate_bare_template_references(
        state_raw,
        state_expanded,
        chain(
            (
                (f"aliases[{key!r}]", value)
                for key, value in (meta_parts[0] or {}).items()
            ),
            ((f"equations[{key!r}]", value) for key, value in equations_map.items()),
        ),
    )

    # Pre-scan raw aliases + equations for shaped-parameter references before
    # alias/template expansion mangles bracketed bases into per-coord names.
    axis_lookup_dict: dict[str, list[str]] = build_axis_lookup(axes_meta)
    aliases_raw_map = meta_parts[0] or {}
    name_blocklist = (
        {parse_selector(s)[0] for s in state_raw}
        | set(state_expanded)
        | {parse_selector(_normalize_bracket_key(k))[0] for k in aliases_raw_map}
        | set(aliases_raw_map.keys())
    )
    raw_expressions: list[str] = [
        v for v in aliases_raw_map.values() if isinstance(v, str)
    ]
    raw_expressions.extend(v for v in equations_map.values() if isinstance(v, str))
    shaped_params = _scan_shaped_param_refs(
        raw_expressions,
        name_blocklist=name_blocklist,
        axis_lookup=axis_lookup_dict,
    )
    _reject_legacy_time_varying_field(spec)
    shaped_params, time_varying_full = _partition_time_varying_shaped(
        shaped_params,
        time_axis_name=time_axis_name,
        axis_lookup=axis_lookup_dict,
    )
    meta.update(
        _normalize_time_metadata(
            spec,
            time_axis_name=time_axis_name,
            axes_meta=axes_meta,
            time_varying_params=time_varying_full,
        )
    )
    if time_varying_full:
        _strip_time_axis_in_mapping(
            equations_map,
            tv_full_axes=time_varying_full,
            time_axis_name=time_axis_name,
        )
        if isinstance(meta_parts[0], dict):
            _strip_time_axis_in_mapping(
                meta_parts[0],
                tv_full_axes=time_varying_full,
                time_axis_name=time_axis_name,
            )

    aliases_ir_map, aliases_ir_reduce_map, alias_template_map = (
        _build_aliases_ir_from_raw(
            meta_parts[0],
            axes=axes_meta,
            shaped_params=shaped_params,
            axis_lookup=axis_lookup_dict,
        )
    )
    template_map_all = {**state_template_map, **alias_template_map}

    chain_block = spec.get("chain")
    if chain_block:
        if not isinstance(chain_block, list):
            raise InvalidRhsSpecError(detail="chain must be a list if provided")
        _apply_expr_chains(
            chains=chain_block,
            state_expanded=state_expanded,
            equations_map=equations_map,
        )

    unknown_keys = [
        k
        for k in equations_map
        if k not in state_expanded and k not in template_map_all
    ]
    if unknown_keys:
        raise InvalidRhsSpecError(
            detail=f"unknown equation key(s): {sorted(unknown_keys)}"
        )

    equations_ir_built, equations_ir_reduce, all_syms = _build_equations_ir_from_raw(
        state_expanded=state_expanded,
        equations_map=equations_map,
        template_map=template_map_all,
        axes=axes_meta,
        shaped_params=shaped_params,
        axis_lookup=axis_lookup_dict,
        aliases_ir=aliases_ir_map,
    )
    # Collect free symbols from alias bodies (alias bodies may reference
    # params not appearing in any equation directly). Walk the *reduce*
    # map (Reduce nodes still folded) rather than the fully expanded
    # map: alias inlining is identical between the two, but the reduce
    # form is orders of magnitude smaller for continuum specs. Share a
    # single id-keyed memo across the per-cell entries so common
    # subtrees are visited at most once (issue #145).
    fs_memo: dict[int, frozenset[str]] = {}
    for alias_ir_val in aliases_ir_reduce_map.values():
        all_syms |= free_symbols(alias_ir_val, memo=fs_memo)

    _maybe_attach_initial_state(
        meta,
        spec.get("initial_state"),
        axes=axes_meta,
        template_map=template_map_all,
    )

    meta["shaped_params"] = tuple(sorted(shaped_params.items()))
    meta["time_axis"] = time_axis_name
    meta["time_varying_params"] = tuple(sorted(time_varying_full.items()))

    factorize_axes_raw = spec.get("factorize_axes")
    if factorize_axes_raw:
        known_axes = {ax["name"] for ax in axes_meta}
        meta["factorize_axes"] = [
            a for a in factorize_axes_raw if isinstance(a, str) and a in known_axes
        ]

    state_set = set(state_expanded)
    shaped_set = set(shaped_params)
    time_varying_set = set(time_varying_full)
    axis_name_set = set(axis_lookup_dict)
    template_base_set = {parse_selector(k)[0] for k in template_map_all}
    # Share an identity-keyed unparse memo between the equation and
    # alias rendering passes so subexpressions that recur across alias
    # bodies and equations (e.g. coord-pinned copies of the same
    # alias template body) are rendered only once (issue #145).
    unparse_memo: dict[tuple[int, int, bool], str] = {}
    equations_strings = _derive_equation_strings_lazy(
        equations_ir_built, _unparse_memo=unparse_memo
    )
    aliases_strings = _derive_alias_strings(
        aliases_ir_map, aliases_ir_map, _unparse_memo=unparse_memo
    )

    param_names = _sorted_unique(
        sym
        for sym in all_syms
        if sym not in state_set
        and sym not in aliases_ir_map
        and sym not in shaped_set
        and sym not in time_varying_set
        and sym not in axis_name_set
        and sym not in template_base_set
        and sym not in _SHAPED_PARAM_BUILTIN_NAMES
    )

    state_templates = _build_state_templates(
        state_raw,
        axes=axes_meta,
        state_template_map=state_template_map,
        state_expanded=state_expanded,
    )
    meta.update(
        _state_declaration_metadata(
            spec.get("state_metadata"),
            templates=state_templates,
            axes=axes_meta,
            state_axes=meta_parts[1],
        )
    )
    normalized = ExprRhs(
        state_names=tuple(state_expanded),
        equations=equations_strings,
        aliases=aliases_strings,
        param_names=param_names,
        all_symbols=frozenset(all_syms | set(aliases_ir_map.keys())),
        meta=meta,
        state_templates=state_templates,
        shaped_params=tuple(sorted(shaped_params.items())),
        time_varying_params=tuple(sorted(time_varying_full.items())),
        aliases_ir=aliases_ir_map,
        equations_ir=equations_ir_built,
        aliases_ir_reduce=aliases_ir_reduce_map,
        equations_ir_reduce=equations_ir_reduce,
        alias_templates=_build_alias_templates(
            aliases_raw_map,
            axes=axes_meta,
            alias_template_map=alias_template_map,
        ),
    )
    return _finish_observables(normalized, spec)

def normalize_rhs(spec: Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> NormalizedRhs:
    """Normalize a RHS specification dict into a backend-facing representation.

    Args:
        spec: Raw RHS specification mapping.

    Returns:
        Backend-facing normalized RHS representation.

    Raises:
        InvalidRhsSpecError: If validation fails.
        UnsupportedFeatureError: If validation fails.
    """
    if spec is None:
        raise InvalidRhsSpecError(detail="rhs specification is required")

    kind = str(spec.get("kind", "expr")).strip().lower()

    if kind == "expr":
        return normalize_expr_rhs(spec)

    if kind == "transitions":
        return normalize_transitions_rhs(spec)

    raise UnsupportedFeatureError(
        feature=f"rhs.kind={kind}",
        detail="Only 'expr' and 'transitions' are supported in v1.",
    )
